blocks.title: MIA — check bags & security
blocks.detail: Arrive about three hours before departure. Bags tag through to Paris on the single Aer Lingus ticket, so this is the only check-in of the outbound.

blocks.title: Aer Lingus 140 · MIA → DUB (overnight)
blocks.detail: 8h15m, Airbus A330-300, landing Dublin Terminal 2 at 8:20 AM. An evening departure means the kids go down close to a normal bedtime.
blocks.program: Aer Lingus award — currency to confirm
blocks.notes: 27,500 points + $29.10 per person. Four passengers = 110,000 points + $116.40. Fare class P, exactly 4 seats showing. Total elapsed MIA→CDG is 11h40m.
blocks.flag: Only 4 award seats — no margin. Confirm the points currency before assuming the balance covers it.

blocks.title: Dublin connection — 1h35m
blocks.detail: Both flights are Aer Lingus out of Terminal 2. Follow Flight Connections signage to passport control. On a single ticket, checked bags move automatically and there is no second security screening.
blocks.flag: Under the 1h45m–2h Aer Lingus recommends for US arrivals continuing into Europe. A late EI140 threatens the Paris leg.

blocks.title: Aer Lingus 524 · DUB → CDG
blocks.detail: 1h50m, Airbus A320, arriving Paris Charles de Gaulle Terminal 1 at 12:45 PM.

blocks.title: CDG arrival — passport control, bags, customs
blocks.detail: Terminal 1. Ireland is outside Schengen, so this is a full external-border arrival with passport control despite the inbound leg being intra-EU. Sixty-five minutes budgeted.

blocks.title: Bags to the taxi rank
blocks.detail: Official rank at Terminal 1 arrivals level. Use the marked rank only.

blocks.title: Taxi CDG → Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile
blocks.detail: Porte Maillot is in the 17th — Right Bank, so the regulated flat rate is €56. Luggage included, no night or passenger surcharge. Roughly 45–60 minutes for the 30 km. Two taxis for four with winter luggage, or request a van.
blocks.notes: No direct bus from CDG to Porte Maillot. Roissybus runs only to Opéra; RER B lands at Châtelet-Les Halles needing a change onto Métro 1 westbound.

blocks.title: Check in — Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile, 4 nights, 2 rooms
blocks.detail: 3 Place du Général Kœnig, 75017 Paris. The tallest hotel in Paris, directly above Porte Maillot and attached to the Palais des Congrès. High south-facing floors have genuine Eiffel Tower views, and the Regency Club lounge has breakfast, all-day refreshments and evening hors d'oeuvres.
blocks.roomType: 2 rooms — high floor, Eiffel Tower view requested
blocks.notes: 15,000 points per room per night × 2 rooms × 4 nights = 120,000. Category 4: 12,000 off-peak / 15,000 standard / 18,000 peak. Porte Maillot underneath serves Métro 1 (direct to the Champs-Élysées, Louvre and Châtelet with no change), RER C, and RER E since its 2024 extension.
blocks.flag: Confirm these dates don't price at Category 4 peak (18,000/night = 144,000 total), and whether Globalist breakfast and Regency Club access extend to the second room.

days.title: Paris — open (early night before the train)

blocks.title: Back at the hotel by 8:15 PM
blocks.detail: Tomorrow is a 5h30 travel day starting with a 09:30 hotel departure. Working back: ready for breakfast 08:15, minus an hour of morning prep, ten hours of sleep and an hour of bedtime routine puts the hard return deadline at 8:15 PM tonight.

blocks.title: Regency Club breakfast & checkout
blocks.detail: No rush — the 10:18 train is the only fixed point of the morning.

blocks.title: Taxi to Gare de Lyon
blocks.detail: Métro 1 runs from directly beneath the hotel to Gare de Lyon with no change in about 25 minutes, but with four people and winter luggage in Monday rush hour a taxi is the softer option at roughly €25–30 — worth it on a day where missing the train breaks the chain.

blocks.title: Gare de Lyon — platform & food for the train
blocks.detail: Platform numbers post about twenty minutes before departure. Buy lunch here; the bar car with four people is not a plan.

blocks.title: TGV Lyria 9765 · Paris Gare de Lyon → Genève Cornavin
blocks.detail: 3h18, calling at Bourg-en-Bresse 12:12 and Bellegarde 12:59. Passports out — this crosses into Switzerland.
blocks.notes: Family estimate with one Carte Avantage Adulte (€49): about €174 for the four of you at a €79 base fare, against €316 without the card. Plus roughly €56 for the bus. Lyria Standard fares open around €49 and climb like an airfare — expect €59–89 if you book on 30 September and €120–180 if you leave it.
blocks.flag: Times are the current-season pattern. The 13 December 2026 timetable recast has not published and sales open 30 September 2026. Re-verify then.

blocks.title: Walk Cornavin → Gare Routière, Place Dorcière
blocks.detail: About 350m via Rue du Mont-Blanc or Rue des Alpes — ten minutes for an adult, so budget fifteen to twenty with two children and bags. City bus 9 or 25 covers it in two stops if the weather is bad. You never need to go near the airport: both FlixBus and Swiss Tours run from the city-centre coach station.

blocks.title: Bus Geneva → Chamonix
blocks.detail: 1h10–1h25 up the valley. FlixBus runs nine city-centre departures a day between 04:35 and 22:35; Swiss Tours runs eleven, 08:00–20:30, and is usually a little cheaper at €11–17 per person. Book FlixBus if you want free cancellation — a late TGV otherwise forfeits the fare.
blocks.flag: No through-ticketing. Do not book a bus departing before about 14:30 — you want an hour of buffer on the Lyria arrival.

blocks.title: Arrive Chamonix Centre — walk to the hotel
blocks.detail: Get off at Chamonix Centre (414 Allée Recteur Payot), not Chamonix Sud — it is next to the SNCF station and about four minutes from the hotel. Chamonix Sud is half a kilometre further out.

blocks.title: Check in — Pointe Isabelle, 6 nights
blocks.detail: 165 Avenue Michel Croz. A 3-star with quadruple rooms of 27–34m², a top-floor sauna with rooftop views, a gym, and a bar-bistro. Two to three minutes from the town centre, four from the station and the Montenvers train, about nine from Les Planards. Ask for the Carte d'Hôte at the desk — free, and it gives unlimited free travel on the Mont-Blanc Express between Servoz and Vallorcine for the whole stay.
blocks.notes: €1,668 for six nights including taxes and fees — roughly €278 a night — live and fully refundable at time of research, discounted from €1,710 with four rooms left. Scores 9.0/10 across 520 reviews. Breakfast is not published; budget about €58 a morning for four on the town benchmark, roughly €350 across the stay, and ask for a B&B rate booking direct. Cheaper alternative: Hôtel La Verticale at €1,511, a plain 2-star two minutes from the centre with no facilities.
blocks.flag: Request a rear-facing room. Several guests report the street side is loud from the bars on Avenue Michel Croz.

blocks.title: Evening stroll — Chamonix centre
blocks.detail: Flat, pedestrianised and lit, starting at the hotel door. Rue du Docteur Paccard and Avenue Michel Croz for the alpine facades and the Christmas lighting. Short loop — everyone has been travelling since breakfast.

blocks.title: Dinner — La Calèche
blocks.detail: 18 rue du Docteur Paccard, four minutes on foot. Savoyard, open since 1946, 310 covers so it absorbs a family without a wait. Real variety beyond cheese: osso bucco €28, mountain sausage with Reblochon cream and purée €28, roast pork chop €29, crozets risotto with Tome des Bauges €26, tartiflette €25. Minis Gourmets children's menu €17.50 — pasta, steak or trout with dessert.
blocks.notes: Two adult mains around €28 plus two children's menus at €17.50 is roughly €91 before drinks. Reserve ahead on 04 50 55 94 68 — this is Christmas week.
blocks.flag: One listing shows Monday closed while the restaurant's own site and the tourist office say open daily. Phone to confirm, and hold the hotel bistro as the fallback.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.detail: Deliberately unhurried. Nothing today is more than ten minutes from the hotel — this is the recovery day after travel, not a day trip.

blocks.title: Chamonix town & the Christmas lights
blocks.detail: The pedestrian centre, the Maison de la Montagne, and the bridges over the Arve with the Aiguilles above. Hot chocolate at Aux Petits Gourmands, 168 rue du Docteur Paccard — thick chocolat chaud, quiches and sandwiches, open every day 07:30–19:30, about nine minutes from the hotel.

blocks.title: Lunch — Le Cap Horn
blocks.detail: 74 rue des Moulins, five minutes from the hotel. The widest genuinely child-friendly menu in town: crispy katsu chicken €30, smash burger of Iberian pork €27, moules €25, fish of the day €26, Angus bavette €30. Children's menu €17 — crispy chicken, fish fillet or steak haché with a side and dessert. Lunch formule €28.
blocks.notes: Roughly €88 before drinks. Reserve on +33 4 50 21 80 80.

blocks.title: Back to the hotel — into snow gear
blocks.detail: Deliberate changeover block. Sledging means snow down collars and wet gloves — everyone changes properly now rather than improvising at the park.

blocks.title: Les Planards — Alpine Coaster & sledging
blocks.detail: 351 chemin du Pied du Grépon, about nine minutes on foot behind the Montenvers station. The coaster runs 1.3 km of banked rail with 540° spirals and each sledge's brake is rider-controlled, so you set the speed. The base area has the town's dedicated toboggan slopes. Coaster runs 11:00–17:30 daily in winter and is lit in the evening over Christmas.
blocks.notes: 6-ride pack €47.50 (5+1 free). Minimum age 3 seated with an adult; minimum height to ride alone is 1.35m, which neither child will meet, so each family descent uses two sledges and the 6-pack buys three descents together. No lift pass is needed for the coaster or the sledging area.
blocks.flag: Sledging-area hours, access price and whether sledges are hired or sold could not be confirmed — the Planards site was down throughout research. Call ahead.

blocks.title: Back to the hotel — dry off, sauna
blocks.detail: Wet gear off and drying. The top-floor sauna has rooftop views and is exactly the right thing after three hours outdoors.

blocks.title: Dinner — hotel bistro
blocks.detail: Downstairs, no walk in the cold at either end after a full afternoon outside.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.detail: The one early start of the stay, and it buys a full day out of the valley.

blocks.title: Walk to Chamonix Sud bus station
blocks.detail: 234 Avenue de Courmayeur, twelve minutes from the hotel. There is also a Chamonix Centre stop at Allée Recteur Payot, four minutes away — check which one your booking uses.

blocks.title: Bus Chamonix → Annecy
blocks.detail: 1h10 direct down the valley and out of the mountains. Arrives at the bus station, 3 Place de la Gare, next to the SNCF station.
blocks.notes: BlaBlaCar Bus from €7.99 with about ten connections a day — cheaper and three times more frequent than FlixBus, and tickets are exchangeable and refundable free up to 30 days out. FlixBus runs three a day from about €11.63. Roughly €64–74 return for the family. Some services stop at Bonlieu, which is two minutes from the Pont des Amours — take that one if offered.
blocks.flag: Individual December departure times are not published yet. The operating window runs 06:00–17:00 outbound and to 22:05 returning, so the day works — but book the exact times as soon as they load.

blocks.title: Pont des Amours, Le Pâquier & the lakefront
blocks.detail: First light and the coldest part of the day, so keep moving. The Pont des Amours crosses the Canal du Vassé between the Pâquier and the Jardins de l'Europe and is the postcard view. Le Pâquier is the big lakeside meadow with swans and ducks year-round — bring seed, not bread. Flat, buggy-friendly, mountains across the water. All free.

blocks.title: The old town & the canals
blocks.detail: The Canal du Thiou, Quai de l'Île, Rue Sainte-Claire and Rue Perrière — arcaded, pedestrian, lit, and strung with Christmas lights in late December. This is what Annecy is famous for and it takes about an hour with children and stops.

blocks.title: Lunch — Chez Mamie Lise
blocks.detail: 11 Rue Grenette, in the old town on the square where Santa's meet-and-greet sits. Open daily 11:45–14:00. Genuinely varied and not a fondue shop: lake perch and char €34.50–35.80, duck, pork and chicken €35.80–39.50, beef tartares from €25.50, salads €15.50–28.50. Children's menu €18 — steak, chicken nuggets or ham with a side and dessert. Plat du jour €19.
blocks.notes: Adult mains here are expensive at €25–40; use the €19 plat du jour to control it. A family lunch runs €100–130. Reserve on +33 4 50 45 41 18.

blocks.title: Jardins de l'Europe & the ice rink
blocks.detail: The lakeside park at the mouth of the Thiou, which in December doubles as the main Christmas market site. A 460m² natural ice rink sits here with skate hire on site, and in prior years a slower zone for young children.
blocks.flag: 2026 rink prices are not published anywhere. Expect roughly €6–8 per person including skates — an estimate, not a verified figure.

blocks.title: Noël des Alpes Christmas market
blocks.detail: Dusk falls about 16:50, which is when the market is at its best. 135 artisan chalets across the town centre and the Jardins de l'Europe, illuminations on the historic buildings, a Santa Claus meet-and-greet, Savoyard food and vin chaud. Free entry. Confirmed dates: 26 November 2026 – 3 January 2027, 11:00–21:00 with later hours Thursday to Saturday.

blocks.title: Bus back to Chamonix
blocks.detail: Return leg. Back in Chamonix around 20:00 — late for the kids, but the market after dark is the whole reason to stay past dusk.

blocks.title: Late supper — hotel bistro
blocks.detail: Downstairs, no walk, no booking needed after a long day.

days.title: Mer de Glace, ice rink & Christmas Eve

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.detail: Everything today is walkable. Nothing leaves the valley on Christmas Eve — deliberate, so a late closure or a thin bus timetable cannot strand anyone.

blocks.title: Walk to the Montenvers station
blocks.detail: Four minutes — the cogwheel station sits immediately beside the SNCF station. Buy at the ticket office, where the family pass and the under-5 exemption get applied.

blocks.title: Montenvers Railway — the red train
blocks.detail: Twenty minutes of cogwheel railway climbing through snow-covered pine to 1,913m, opening onto the Mer de Glace. First train of the day — worth it for the light and the empty platforms.
blocks.notes: Voyage Mer de Glace family pass €148.30 covers two adults and two children for train, gondola, ice cave and museums. Individually it would be €183.80, so the family pass saves about €35. Age bands: adult 15–64, child 5–14, under 5 free with proof of age at the ticket office.
blocks.flag: Winter 2026/27 fares are not published — these are prior-season figures. Expect 3–5% higher.

blocks.title: Gondola down & the Grotte de Glace
blocks.detail: Gondola from 1,913m down to 1,760m, then a staircase to the cave mouth carved fresh into the glacier each autumn. About 170 steps down and the same back up — roughly a ten-storey climb on open metal treads that can ice up. Hold hands, and expect to carry the 5-year-old part of the way back. No pushchairs, no lift alternative.
blocks.flag: The ice cave opens only days before you arrive — indicated from 13 December, but in 2025/26 it slipped to the 20th. Re-verify in late November. The train and the glacier viewpoint stand on their own if it has not opened.

blocks.title: Train back down
blocks.detail: Twenty minutes. Last ascent is 16:00 and last descent 16:30, so there is no pressure this early.

blocks.title: Lunch — Aux Petits Gourmands
blocks.detail: 168 rue du Docteur Paccard, nine minutes on foot. Pâtisserie and tea salon with real savoury options — quiches, sandwiches, salads — so it works as a lunch rather than a sugar stop. The Christmas chocolate displays are the draw for the kids.

blocks.title: Back to the hotel — thick socks for the rink
blocks.detail: Changeover block. Snow gear off and drying, normal clothes and proper socks on.

blocks.title: Ice skating — Patinoire Richard Bozon
blocks.detail: 214 avenue de la Plage, about fifteen minutes on foot or one stop on the bus to Médiathèque. Olympic-size indoor rink, 60m × 30m. Public session runs 14:00–18:00 daily through the holiday period.
blocks.notes: Entry €6.80 adult, €5.00 child, under 6 free — so the 5-year-old is free and the 7-year-old pays €5. Skate hire €4.50 each. About €36.60 for four. The Carte d'Hôte gets a reduced rate.
blocks.flag: Whether this rink has penguin-style support frames could not be confirmed — they are documented at the Les Houches rink, not this one. Phone +33 4 50 53 12 36. The rink has also not published 24 December hours; assume it may close early.

blocks.title: Back to the hotel — warm up and change
blocks.detail: Unstructured, then into something decent for Christmas Eve dinner.

blocks.title: Christmas Eve dinner
blocks.detail: Chamonix restaurants run fixed festive menus on the 24th and they sell out. Book in November. Le Cap Horn runs a festive service every season; Pointe Isabelle (the restaurant, 165 Avenue Michel Croz — no relation to the hotel) publishes separate 24 and 25 December menus and is the strongest candidate for both nights.
blocks.notes: Chamonix norms for 24 December run €70–120 per adult with à la carte withdrawn, and several venues offer no child price at all.
blocks.flag: No Chamonix venue has published 2026 festive menus — they appear early-to-mid November. Call Le Cap Horn (+33 4 50 21 80 80) and Pointe Isabelle (+33 4 50 53 12 87) the week they open.

blocks.title: Breakfast & presents
blocks.detail: No fixed start today. The pool is confirmed closed, the rink has not published hours, and most shops shut — so the day is built around things that cannot close: lifts, snow and the valley train.

blocks.title: Walk to the Planpraz gondola
blocks.detail: The Brévent–Planpraz base is on the north edge of the centre, about ten minutes from the hotel. Walkable, no bus needed.

blocks.title: Gondola to Planpraz, 2,000m
blocks.detail: A sun-facing shelf directly opposite Mont Blanc — the classic postcard angle, with the whole massif across the valley. Lifts run on Christmas Day; it is their peak revenue week.
blocks.notes: Pedestrian return Chamonix→Planpraz: family pass €77.60, or adult €25.00 and child 5–14 €18.00 individually. Under 5 free. Adding the top section to Brévent at 2,525m is a further €18.00 adult and €15.30 child — colder, windier, and not worth it with small kids.
blocks.flag: Fares shown are the summer 2026 sheet; the winter grid publishes around November.

blocks.title: Snow play at Planpraz
blocks.detail: Deep snow, wide open ground and a big sunny terrace, with the valley floor a thousand metres below. Snowmen, snowball fights, and room to run. Being straight about what this is: Planpraz is a ski-area mid-station, not a snow park — there is no toboggan run here, so don't promise the kids sledging. Tuesday at Les Planards was the sledging.

blocks.title: Lunch — La Bergerie de Planpraz
blocks.detail: The mountain restaurant at the top station, so no descending for lunch. Somewhere warm to dry gloves and get hot food in before heading down.
blocks.notes: Mountain-restaurant pricing in a French ski area on Christmas Day runs high — budget €25–30 per adult main and €15–18 for children. The 2026/27 menu is not published; treat as an estimate.
blocks.flag: Confirm it is open on 25 December — mountain restaurants usually are during the holiday week, but it has not been verified.

blocks.title: Gondola down
blocks.detail: Last descent is 17:00, so no pressure.

blocks.title: Mont-Blanc Express to Argentière — free
blocks.detail: The Carte d'Hôte makes the valley train free between Servoz and Vallorcine, so this costs nothing and needs no tickets. Argentière is fifteen minutes up the line at 1,250m — a smaller, quieter village under the Aiguille Verte, deeper snow than Chamonix, and an easy walk around. Turn-up-and-go, and come back whenever everyone has had enough.

blocks.title: Christmas dinner
blocks.detail: Book in November alongside Christmas Eve. Far fewer places open on the 25th than the 24th, and those that do run a fixed lunch or dinner menu at a set price.
blocks.flag: Christmas Day is the hardest booking of the trip. Pointe Isabelle restaurant publishes a separate 25 December menu — call +33 4 50 53 12 87 in November.

blocks.title: Breakfast & passports
blocks.detail: Passports for all four today. France and Italy are both in Schengen so there are no routine checks at the tunnel, but the bus operators require ID and random checks happen.

blocks.title: Walk to Chamonix Sud bus station
blocks.detail: 234 Avenue de Courmayeur, about twelve minutes from the hotel. The SAT Mont Blanc coach leaves from here.

blocks.title: SAT bus · Chamonix → Courmayeur
blocks.detail: About 45 minutes through the 11.6 km Mont Blanc tunnel to Piazzale Monte Bianco. You emerge in Italy — different language, different food, same mountain from the other side.
blocks.notes: €30 adult / €15 child 0–12 same-day return = €90 for the family. Booking is MANDATORY by 17:00 the previous day — which is Christmas Day — via savda.it or estore.arriva.it, so book it on the 23rd or 24th instead of leaving it. FlixBus also runs the route five times a day from about €12, but those are long-haul Geneva–Turin coaches whose timings suit the through route rather than day-trippers.
blocks.flag: Book the SAT bus by 17:00 on 25 December at the latest, and preferably several days earlier — the deadline falls on Christmas Day. The winter 2026/27 timetable is not published — phone +33 4 50 78 05 33 or +39 0165 367039 for the actual departure times.

blocks.title: Fun Park Dolonne — tubing & bobsled track
blocks.detail: Strada Chécrouit 9. This is the day's anchor and the reason to come: a proper tubing run and a bobsled/sledge track, plus a play area with soft inflatables, trampolines, carousels and slides for when the 5-year-old has had enough of the cold. There is also a beginner slope with three magic-carpet conveyor lifts if anyone wants a first-ever go on skis. Café on site.
blocks.notes: Neither Chamonix nor the French side of the valley has a dedicated tubing run — this is the only one within reach. Prices are not published; a family blogger reports you can pay per activity rather than buying a full day pass, which suits a half-day visit.
blocks.flag: Prices, hours and minimum ages all unpublished. Phone +39 366 268 6776 or email funpark.dolonne@gmail.com before travelling.

blocks.title: Lunch on Via Roma
blocks.detail: Courmayeur's pedestrian main street — genuinely Italian rather than French-alpine, which after two days of Savoyard food is the point. Pizza, pasta, gelato even in December.

blocks.title: Via Roma & the village
blocks.detail: Unstructured. Shops, hot chocolate, the church square, Mont Blanc from the Italian side. Deliberately no second ticketed activity — the morning was the event.

blocks.title: SAT bus back to Chamonix
blocks.detail: Return leg of the same booking. Back at Chamonix Sud around 16:30, twelve minutes' walk from the hotel.

blocks.title: Dinner — Bighorn Bistro & Bakery
blocks.detail: 77 place Edmond Desailloud. Family-run American bistro that bakes its own bread: Bighorn burger €20, Peruvian chicken burger €20, Savoyard mac & cheese €15, farm/sea/forest bowls €18, sticky BBQ pork ribs €39. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options. Open Saturday from 16:00; it closes Monday and Tuesday, so this is one of the nights it is available.
blocks.notes: Roughly €65–70 for four. Reservations recommended on +33 7 89 07 79 62. A kids' menu exists but the price is not published.

blocks.title: Breakfast & pack
blocks.detail: Unhurried. Checkout is 11:00 and the bus is not until midday.

blocks.title: Checkout — and buy the bus ticket online
blocks.detail: Critical: Chamonix Sud bus station is unstaffed on Sundays with no ticket machines. Buy the Geneva ticket online before leaving the hotel.
blocks.flag: Do not plan to buy the bus ticket at the station. There is nobody there on a Sunday.

blocks.title: Walk to Chamonix Sud
blocks.detail: Twelve minutes with luggage. Taxi fallback +33 4 50 53 13 94.

blocks.title: Bus Chamonix → Genève, Place Dorcière
blocks.detail: 1h20 back down the valley. Allow a generous buffer — the Chamonix–Geneva road on a changeover Sunday in the ski season can add thirty minutes or more.

blocks.title: Walk Place Dorcière → Genève Cornavin
blocks.detail: 350m, fifteen to twenty minutes with children and luggage. Lyria advises extra time boarding at Geneva because of border formalities — have documents out.

blocks.title: TGV Lyria 9774 · Genève → Paris Gare de Lyon
blocks.detail: 3h15, calling at Bellegarde 15:02. Arrives Gare de Lyon 17:42.
blocks.notes: Same Carte Avantage discounts as the outbound — roughly €174 for the four of you plus about €56 for the bus.
blocks.flag: Sunday loses three of the eight Geneva–Paris departures: no 06:28, 10:27 or 12:27, leaving a six-hour hole between 08:21 and 14:27. The 14:27 is the only civilised option. Book it the moment sales open on 30 September — this is the tightest capacity point of the trip. Fallback is the 16:23, arriving 19:42.

blocks.title: Gare de Lyon — bags to the taxi rank
blocks.detail: Straight out to the rank on the Boulevard Diderot side.

blocks.title: Taxi Gare de Lyon → Hyatt House CDG
blocks.detail: Roughly 35 km north-east, 45–60 minutes on a Sunday evening. The regulated CDG flat rate does not apply in this direction to a hotel outside the airport perimeter, so expect a metered fare around €70–90. RER D to Gare du Nord then RER B to CDG is the cheap alternative at about an hour, but with four people, luggage and a long day behind you the taxi is worth it.
blocks.flag: Fare is an estimate — metered, not flat-rate, and Sunday evening traffic varies. Confirm whether the hotel runs an airport shuttle you could pick up instead.

blocks.title: Check in — Hyatt House Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport
blocks.detail: Airport hotel for the night before the flight home. Kitchenette-equipped suites, free airport shuttle, and about fifteen minutes from the terminals.
blocks.notes: 15,000 points for the night as given.
blocks.flag: Confirm whether 15,000 covers one room or two. The Paris stay uses two rooms; if this night needs two as well, it is 30,000. Also confirm the shuttle timetable for a 9:10 AM departure — you will need to be at CDG by about 06:40.

blocks.title: Dinner at the hotel
blocks.detail: No excursion tonight. Bags repacked, boarding passes out, early night.

blocks.title: Wake, pack, hotel shuttle
blocks.detail: Aiming to be at the terminal by about 06:40 for a 9:10 departure — roughly two and a half hours for a transatlantic with four people and checked bags.

blocks.title: Shuttle to CDG
blocks.detail: Free hotel shuttle, about fifteen minutes. Confirm the first departure time at check-in the night before — if it runs later than 06:15, book a taxi instead.
blocks.flag: Verify the shuttle's first run. An airport hotel shuttle that starts at 07:00 does not work for a 9:10 flight.

blocks.title: CDG — check in, security, passport control
blocks.detail: Delta departs from Terminal 2E. Schengen exit control plus US-bound security screening — allow the full window.

blocks.title: Delta 83 · CDG → Atlanta
blocks.detail: Transatlantic leg, arriving Atlanta early afternoon local time.
blocks.notes: 60,000 SkyMiles + €117 per person. Four passengers = 240,000 SkyMiles + €468 (about $543). Fare class NL, 9 seats showing. Total elapsed CDG→MIA is 16h05 with a 3h47 layover in Atlanta.
blocks.flag: This is more than double the outbound award — 240,000 SkyMiles against 110,000 on Aer Lingus. The same Delta metal may be bookable through Virgin Atlantic or Air France/KLM Flying Blue for materially fewer points. Worth pricing both before spending 240K.

blocks.title: Atlanta — 3h47 layover
blocks.detail: US immigration and customs happen here, not in Miami — first port of entry. Recheck bags after customs, then back through security to the domestic concourse. The long layover is doing real work: it absorbs the immigration queue without putting the Miami leg at risk.

blocks.title: Delta 1328 · Atlanta → Miami
blocks.detail: Home, arriving 7:15 PM.

ideas.title: ⚠ TRIP-BREAKER — Leavenworth collision
ideas.detail: This trip is Dec 16–28, 2026. Leavenworth Winter 2026 is Dec 19–27, 2026 with MIA→SEA booked on Dec 19 (Alaska AS305, conf UUKHNQ) and a Hampton Inn on 308K Hilton points. They overlap by eight days and both depart from Miami. These cannot both happen. Nothing here should be booked until one of them moves.

ideas.title: ⚠ BOOK 30 SEPTEMBER — the whole rail spine
ideas.detail: SNCF opens sales for 13 Dec 2026 – 6 Jan 2027 on Wednesday 30 September 2026, around 05:45. Both TGV Lyria legs depend on it. Buy a Carte Avantage Adulte (€49) BEFORE booking — it gives −30% to the holder and one companion adult and −60% for both children aged 4–11, turning roughly €316 of one-way fares into about €174. Note the €89 capped fare does NOT apply on Lyria: SNCF guarantees those caps on domestic TGV INOUI and INTERCITÉS only, and Lyria is a separate Franco-Swiss operation.

ideas.title: ⚠ Sunday 27 December loses three of eight Geneva–Paris trains
ideas.detail: On Sundays the 06:28, 10:27 and 12:27 Geneva departures do not run, leaving a six-hour hole between 08:21 and 14:27 — exactly the slot a family checking out of a hotel wants, on the last Sunday of the French school holidays when the whole valley turns over. The 14:27 is the plan. It is the tightest capacity point of the trip: book it first.

ideas.title: ⚠ Chamonix Sud bus station is unstaffed on Sundays
ideas.detail: No ticket machines, no counter. Buy the Chamonix → Geneva bus ticket online before leaving the hotel on the 27th.

ideas.title: No through-ticketing Paris→Chamonix
ideas.detail: The TGV and the bus are separate contracts. A late Lyria forfeits the bus fare with no protection. Leave at least an hour between booked arrival and bus departure, and book the bus on FlixBus, which allows free cancellation and cheap rebooking.

ideas.title: Return flight is 4 × 60,000 SkyMiles
ideas.detail: The Delta award shows 60,000 points + €117 per person. For four that is 240,000 SkyMiles + €468 — more than double the outbound Aer Lingus award. Nine seats showing at NL fare. Worth checking Virgin Atlantic and Air France/KLM Flying Blue as alternative ways to book the same Delta metal before spending 240K.

ideas.title: Hyatt House CDG — confirm one room or two
ideas.detail: Modeled at 15,000 points as given. The Paris stay uses two rooms; if the airport night also needs two, that is 30,000. Confirm before counting the balance.

ideas.title: Passports for everyone, including both children
ideas.detail: The Geneva legs cross into Switzerland, and the Courmayeur day trip crosses into Italy. Switzerland is in Schengen but not the EU customs union, so the border is staffed and spot-checks happen; France has also reintroduced temporary internal Schengen checks. Bus operators on the Courmayeur run require ID regardless. Every traveller needs their own document — a child can no longer travel on a parent's passport.

ideas.title: Courmayeur must be booked the day before
ideas.detail: The SAT Mont Blanc bus requires a reservation by 17:00 the previous day via savda.it or estore.arriva.it. €30 adult / €15 child return, about 45 minutes through the Mont Blanc tunnel.

ideas.title: Fun Park Dolonne is the tubing fix
ideas.detail: Chamonix and the whole Italian upper Val di Susa have no dedicated tubing run. Fun Park Dolonne at Courmayeur has a tubing run, a bobsled track, a beginner slope with magic-carpet lifts, and a soft-play area with inflatables and trampolines. Prices are not published — you can reportedly pay per activity rather than buying a day pass, which suits a half-day visit. Call +39 366 268 6776 to confirm.

ideas.title: Alpine Coaster — both kids ride with an adult
ideas.detail: Minimum age 4; minimum height to ride alone is 1.35m, which neither child will meet. So one family descent uses two sledges. The 6-ride card at €47.50 buys three descents together. Runs 11:00–17:30 daily in winter and is lit in the evening over Christmas.

ideas.title: Ice cave opens only days before arrival
ideas.detail: The Mer de Glace ice cave is re-carved each autumn and does not open with the train. Montenvers indicates the ice-cave combination from 13 December; in 2025/26 it slipped to 20 December. Re-verify in late November. The train and the glacier viewpoint stand on their own if it has not opened.

ideas.title: Christmas Day closures
ideas.detail: The Richard Bozon pool is confirmed closed all day on 25 December and closes at 18:00 on the 24th. The ice rink in the same building has not published 24/25 December hours — phone +33 4 50 53 12 36. Lifts and Les Planards run: it is their peak revenue week. Most shops and many restaurants close on the 25th — book Christmas lunch in advance.

ideas.title: Carte d'Hôte — free valley trains
ideas.detail: Free at check-in. Gives unlimited free travel on the Mont-Blanc Express between Servoz and Vallorcine, covering Les Houches, Les Praz, Argentière and Vallorcine. Turn-up-and-go with no tickets is genuinely useful with young kids — you can bail home whenever someone melts down. Since the December 2023 network relaunch it is NOT a bus ticket, only a discount on Chamonix Mobilité passes.

ideas.title: Request a rear-facing room at Pointe Isabelle
ideas.detail: Several guests report street-facing rooms are loud from the bars on Avenue Michel Croz — one wrote that customers 'scream like hysterics until late at night'. Ask for a courtyard or rear-facing quadruple when booking.

ideas.title: Breakfast is extra almost everywhere in Chamonix
ideas.detail: No Chamonix hotel on the shortlist publishes a breakfast price. The town benchmark (Hôtel L'Oustalet, the only property with a public rate card) is €17 buffet / €14 continental per adult and €12 for children 7–13. Budget roughly €58 a morning for the four of you, about €350 across the stay, and ask Pointe Isabelle for a B&B rate when booking direct.

ideas.title: Annecy is forecast-dependent
ideas.detail: Annecy sits at 447m in a basin prone to winter temperature inversions — you can leave a bright Chamonix morning and arrive in flat grey fog. December averages 7°C, ~57% cloud cover and a 30% chance of a wet day. The whole appeal is outdoors, and the château and Palais de l'Île are ruled out as museums, so there is no wet-weather fallback. Decide 48 hours out on the forecast; if it is raining or fogged in, swap the day for something local.

ideas.title: Confirm the Paris award rate doesn't price peak
ideas.detail: 15,000 points per night is the Category 4 standard rate at the Hyatt Regency Étoile. Category 4 peak is 18,000, and the week before Christmas is a plausible peak window. Across two rooms and four nights that is the difference between 120,000 and 144,000 points.

ideas.title: Globalist benefits on the second Paris room
ideas.detail: Regency Club access and breakfast attach to the room the member occupies. A second room does not automatically carry them. Confirm with the hotel, or check whether a Guest of Honor booking covers it, before assuming breakfast for four.

ideas.title: Aer Lingus award space is exactly four seats
ideas.detail: 4 seats at 27,500 points + $29.10 each — no margin. 110,000 points + $116.40 for the family. Confirm which currency this prices in (Avios is the likely route on Aer Lingus metal).

ideas.title: Dublin connection is under the recommended window
ideas.detail: 1h35m at DUB against the 1h45m–2h Aer Lingus recommends for US arrivals continuing into Europe. Bags transfer automatically on a single ticket and there is no second security screening, but passport control is required and it is the whole widebody queuing at once.

ideas.title: Calls to make in November
ideas.detail: Les Planards for the Alpine Coaster's Christmas-week hours and whether sledges are hired or sold. The Patinoire (+33 4 50 53 12 36) for winter hours, 24/25 December opening, and whether they have support frames for young children. Montenvers for the ice cave's actual opening date. Fun Park Dolonne (+39 366 268 6776) for prices and hours. And the Chamonix tourist office (+33 4 50 53 00 24) for the Christmas programme, which is not published until late November.
